title: Lookalikes
text: Two spiral shells, one ancient and one alive today, look almost identical.
nxt: But here is the surprise: ammonites and the nautilus were not close relatives. So why do they look so alike? Let's find out.

title: Lookalikes
text: But here is the surprise: ammonites and the nautilus were not close relatives. So why do they look so alike? Let's find out.
prev: Two spiral shells, one ancient and one alive today, look almost identical.

title: Different Branches
text: The nautilus belongs to the nautiloids, a branch of cephalopods that split off very early.
nxt: Scientists place ammonites closer to modern squid, cuttlefish, and octopuses than to the nautilus. That means an ammonite was a closer relative of a squid than of a nautilus.

title: Convergent Evolution
text: Their matching spirals are a classic case of convergent evolution, where separate lineages end up with a similar design.
nxt: In nature, looking alike does not always mean being related, and this pair is one of the best examples.

title: The Tube Inside
text: Cut either shell in half, and the differences begin to show. Both are divided into chambers, linked by a thin tube called the siphuncle.
nxt: It helps the animal adjust its buoyancy, a bit like the ballast tank of a submarine.

title: The Tube Inside
text: It helps the animal adjust its buoyancy, a bit like the ballast tank of a submarine.
prev: Cut either shell in half, and the differences begin to show. Both are divided into chambers, linked by a thin tube called the siphuncle.
nxt: In the nautilus, that tube runs through the middle of each chamber wall. In ammonites, it usually ran along the outer edge of the shell.

title: Folded Walls
text: The chamber walls differ too. A nautilus builds simple, smooth, dome-shaped walls.
nxt: Ammonites built walls with elaborate, fractal-like folds along their edges.

title: Folded Walls

nxt: Where those folds meet the shell, they leave wavy lines called sutures, which look like frozen leaves or snowflakes in stone.

title: Why So Complex
text: Why did ammonites evolve such complicated patterns? Scientists are still debating it.
nxt: One idea is that the folds helped strengthen thin shells against water pressure.

title: Tough Survivors
text: And ammonites were tough. About two hundred fifty-two million years ago, the worst mass extinction of all reduced them to only a few lineages, and they rebounded.
nxt: They were hit hard again at the end of the Triassic, and recovered again.

title: Full Story
text: So when ammonites vanished sixty-six million years ago, it was not because they were weak.
